record.original_question: What is the complexity of the problem of determining whether a regular F -factorization possesses synchronization property if the parameters of the synchronization are not given ? What about this problem for context-free F -factorizations?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the problem of determining whether a regular F -factorization possesses synchronization property if the parameters of the synchronization are not given ? What about this problem for context-free F -factorizations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and let $F \subseteq \Sigma^*$ be a language. An $F$-factorization of a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ is a decomposition $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$ with each factor $u_i \in F$. A language $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ is said to admit an $F$-factorization if every $w \in L$ can be written as a concatenation of words from $F$.

Fix integers $m \geq 1$ and $d \geq 0$ (called synchronization parameters). An $F$-factorization $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k$ of a word $w$ is said to have the $(m,d)$-synchronization property if, for every position $i \geq m$ in $w$, any two $F$-factorizations of $w$ agree on whether $i$ is a factor boundary, after looking at a window of length $d$ around $i$. More generally, an $F$-factorization scheme has the synchronization property if there exist parameters $(m,d)$ such that the above holds for all words admitting an $F$-factorization.

Question: Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem.
(a) Regular case: Given a regular language $F$ (specified, say, by a finite automaton or regular expression), decide whether the $F$-factorization possesses the synchronization property, where the parameters $(m,d)$ of the synchronization are not given as part of the input but are existentially quantified.
(b) Context-free case: The same decision problem when $F$ is given as a context-free language (e.g., by a context-free grammar).
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a specific resolution of the complexity of deciding whether a regular or context-free F-factorization possesses the synchronization property when synchronization parameters are not given. Related work exists on synchronized context-free languages and constrained synchronization complexity, but no direct answer to this specific decision problem was found.

status_evidence.title: On the Computational Complexity of Synchronized Context-Free Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes space and time complexity of membership and emptiness problems for synchronized context-free languages.
status_evidence.claim: Related complexity results exist for synchronized context-free languages but do not directly address the specific synchronization-property decision problem for F-factorizations.

status_evidence.title: Computational Complexity of Synchronization Under Sparse Regular Constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Constrained synchronization for sparse regular constraint languages can be NP-complete or polynomial-time depending on the constraint.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates active study of synchronization complexity under regular constraints, without solving the F-factorization synchronization problem in question.
